subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should explicit sessions_send/inter_session delivery requests be solved now with the narrow requester-return/message-tool path, or held for a broader structured delivery-intent contract?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear, but the fix changes model-facing A2A delivery semantics and overlaps an open PR plus broader structured handoff API work, so automation should not choose the product/API direction alone.

options.title: Repair and land the requester-return path
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the near-term fix after its prompt-cache, redaction, and review concerns are resolved, while keeping structured handoff work as follow-up acceptance coverage.

options.title: Design a typed delivery-intent contract first
options.body: Pause the narrow prompt repair and define an additive sessions_send/handoff action that distinguishes delivery requests from coordination chatter before implementation.

options.title: Fold this into the broader handoff issue
options.body: Keep the symptom tracked only through https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 if maintainers decide the WhatsApp case should not be fixed separately.

recommendation.title: Repair and land the requester-return path
recommendation.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 as the near-term fix after its prompt-cache, redaction, and review concerns are resolved, while keeping structured handoff work as follow-up acceptance coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest feature-history signal in the sessions_send/A2A path and already gave maintainer triage direction on the related structured handoff issue.
